requirement.statement: In the LOFT Flow Sheet view, the MD/Eff AUR metric does not respect the correct ticket price and discount. For weeks/channels that have NO Corp Discount override, the Flow Sheet computes AUR off the full-price (FP/pre-MD) ticket instead of the MD ticket, so Flow Sheet AUR != Pricing view AUR. When a channel-level override IS present, that channel uses the MD ticket correctly, producing a blended (partly-right) number. The Pricing view is correct; the Flow Sheet is wrong.
requirement.acceptance: Flow Sheet Eff AUR (ttl + Stores + Ecom) matches the Pricing view for weeks with no override, with a lower-than-default override, and with a higher-than-default override.

evidence.claim: The Pricing view recomputes off the corp markdown calendar: PricingOvertime joins l_corpdisc_tbl / CORPDISC ON week AND prodlife, so an MD-calendar week picks the MD corpdisc row and MD ticket regardless of the plan engine's md_seq. FlowSheetPlanPivot and PricingOvertime BOTH read p_flowsheet, but Pricing re-derives price/discount by prodlife while Flow Sheet shows the stored eff_aur.

Planner channel override path: p_channeloverride/p_itemprice carry a planner 'eff_aur' (expressed_aur) + addoff per product/location/time; these feed adjust_for_md via temp_itemprice_week. When present in the md_seq=0 branch, multiIf(expressed_aur>0, expressed_aur, original_ticketchannel) replaces the FP ticket -> matches Pricing. least(A,B) still picks FP-anchored A when the override discount is SMALLER than corp default (expressed_aur higher), explaining 'only a larger override on all channels makes the views match'.

hypotheses.cause: PRIMARY: The plan-engine effective-AUR formula in p1_08 (adjust_for_md) decides 'is this a markdown week' from md_seq (the erlstmkdnwk / MD-strategy sequence) instead of the corp markdown calendar (l_corpdisc_tbl prodlife='FP'/'MD') that the Pricing view uses. Term A is always anchored to original_ticketchannel (the FP/pre-MD ticket). So for a week where corp markdown is already in effect (MD ticket exists, Pricing correct) but md_seq is still 0 and there is no channel override, least(A,B) resolves to the FP ticket and Flow Sheet AUR is computed off the pre-MD ticket. A channel override injects the planner's expressed_aur and masks the bug for that channel/week; least(A,B) still keeps the FP anchor when the override discount is below the corp default.

Contributing: even in the md_seq>0 branch, term A uses original_ticketchannel*(1-md_corpexcl) (FP ticket, comment says 'CurP for MD') rather than the MD-adjusted ticket, and md_disc is taken from the generic MD-strategy curve ('Normal 20-40-60'), not the actual corp markdown %, so the plan-engine MD ticket can still disagree with the corp MD ticket the Pricing view shows.
RULED OUT - Flow Sheet grid viewdefn display formula: the grid binds raw ttl_eff_aur/eff_aur/eff_aur_ecom with no expression, so the defect is upstream in the pivot/plan-engine, not the view.

root_cause.statement: Flow Sheet Eff AUR / Stores Eff AUR / ECOM Eff AUR are the raw eff_aur / eff_aur_ecom values the plan engine writes to p_flowsheet. The plan-engine AUR formula (loft-configs/pivot/include/p1_08_price_cost_computation.ftl, table adjust_for_md, lines 273-282) computes the ticket base as least(A,B) where A is always anchored to original_ticketchannel (the FP / pre-MD ticket) and the switch to the marked-down ticket happens only when md_seq>0 (driven by erlstmkdnwk + the l_mdstrategy curve) OR a channel override supplies expressed_aur. The Pricing view instead re-derives price and discount from the corp markdown calendar (l_corpdisc_tbl joined on week+prodlife) and is correct. When corp markdown is in effect for a week but the plan engine's md_seq is still 0 and no channel override exists, least(A,B) falls back to the FP ticket, so Flow Sheet AUR is computed off the pre-MD ticket ($39.95) while Pricing uses the MD ticket ($29.96). Reproduced numerically: 39.95*0.96*(1-0.5) = $19.18 (Flow Sheet, wrong) vs 29.96*0.96*(1-0.5) = $14.38 (Pricing, right).
